surface.opening_scene: Nia reviews the authentication logs for her latest piece—every emotional input, every AI iteration, every curatorial decision documented on-chain. In a world where synthetic and human-made are often indistinguishable, provenance has become the art world's obsession. She wonders if anyone actually watches these logs, or if they just need to know they exist.

visible_elements.name: The Artist
visible_elements.description: A celebrated artist navigating the authentication-obsessed art world, known for radical transparency about her human-AI collaborative process.

properties.reputation: respected for both craft and transparency

visible_elements.name: The Authenticated Studio
visible_elements.description: A Tribeca loft where every creative act is logged—neural inputs, AI generations, human selections. The documentation is as much a part of the work as the output.

visible_elements.name: Creative Authentication Protocol
visible_elements.description: System that logs every step of the creative process—emotional inputs, AI outputs, human decisions—creating an immutable record of how a piece came to be.

foundation.core_premise: When AI can generate work indistinguishable from human-made, the art world's response is radical documentation—every creative act logged, every human decision recorded. Authenticity is no longer about whether a human made it, but about the legibility of the process. The question shifts from 'is it real?' to 'can we see how it was made?'

rules.statement: AI-generated work is visually/experientially indistinguishable from human-made work at the output level—only process documentation reveals the difference.
Major collectors and institutions require authentication logs—unlogged work trades at significant discount or is excluded from serious venues.
Some artists resist documentation, arguing it kills mystique and reduces art to process. They operate in parallel markets.
The logs themselves have become aesthetic objects—some collectors care more about beautiful process than beautiful output.

timeline.significance: Triggers first authenticity crisis in visual arts

First widely-adopted standard for process documentation

timeline.significance: Two parallel art worlds develop with different values
Meta-turn where the logs become the work

values: human decision-making as the valuable element
practices: publishing process logs alongside finished work
social_norms: asking about documentation practices is acceptable
undocumented work is viewed with suspicion in mainstream venues
some consider heavy documentation performative or pretentious

systems.name: Creative Authentication Protocol
systems.how_it_works: Continuous logging system that records neural interface inputs, AI system outputs, human selection/rejection decisions, and editing actions. Creates immutable record stored on distributed ledger.
systems.limitations: Cannot capture intention or meaning—only actions. Skilled forgers can generate plausible fake logs. Some argue it documents the wrong things.

systems.name: Logged Neural Interface
systems.how_it_works: Standard emotional-reading interface with authentication layer that timestamps and hashes all inputs, proving a human was emotionally engaged during creation.
systems.limitations: Proves human involvement but not human creativity—you could be bored while technically creating.

systems.name: Provenance Viewer
systems.how_it_works: Interface for experiencing art that includes optional overlay showing the authentication log—viewers can see exactly how each element was created while experiencing the piece.
systems.limitations: Some find the overlay distracting. Others find it more interesting than the art itself.

tentative_ideas: A collector who only cares about logs, barely looks at the actual art
An artist who games the system—creates authentic-looking logs for AI-generated work
Nia's ambivalence about documentation as performance vs. genuine transparency
questions: Does radical transparency enhance or diminish the art experience?
Is documented process just another layer of aesthetic choice?

constraints.description: AI output is indistinguishable from human output at the perceptual level
Authentication logs can prove human involvement but not human creativity or intention
The art world is divided on documentation—neither side has won
Forgery of logs is possible with effort—no system is perfectly secure
